key_insight: CauTrace links ordinary reasoning errors and adversarially induced failures through internal dynamics of support, commitment, and verification.
engineering_relevance: White-box diagnostics can help engineers investigate how LLM failures develop rather than relying only on final-output correctness or safety labels.
method: Define seven functional states for support and constraint processing.
Track how state-related representation changes persist across Transformer blocks.
Analyze support, commitment, and verification timing alongside reasoning-trajectory topology.
evidence_signal: Across Qwen and LLaMA-family models, clean and adversarial failure traces showed weaker Attention–MLP agreement on support-state updates and less verification relative to commitment; held-out repair and steering tests provided supporting signals in specific settings.
watch_item: The approach requires internal model access, and representation signatures and timing shifts vary by architecture, limiting direct transfer of diagnostics or steering interventions.
paper_title: Uncovering Why LLMs Fail: From Internal Mechanisms to Adversarial Reasoning Trajectories
